title: Traction: How Any Startup Can Achieve Explosive Customer Growth (Gabriel Weinberg and Justin Mares)
supports: The book, its authors and UK paperback date (29 October 2015); its case for spending about half of effort on traction, the 19 channels and the testing framework (Bullseye) that the Traction mega pack applies

title: Hacking Growth: How Today's Fastest-Growing Companies Drive Breakout Success (Morgan Brown and Sean Ellis)
supports: The book and its April 2017 date; its focus on acquiring, retaining, engaging and monetising customers through cross-functional teams and continuous testing

title: Four Fits for $100M+ Growth (Brian Balfour)
supports: Market-product, product-channel, channel-model and model-market fit; products are built to fit channels; the fits change and must be revisited

title: The Law of Shitty Clickthroughs (Andrew Chen)
supports: Channels decay as they are copied and scaled; banner click-through fell from about 78% (HotWired, 1994) to about 0.05% (Facebook, 2011); small early tests overstate results at scale

title: The Lean Startup: Methodology (Eric Ries)
supports: Build-measure-learn, minimum viable product, validated learning, innovation accounting and pivot or persevere

title: Startup Metrics for Pirates (Dave McClure, slide deck)
supports: The AARRR stages: acquisition, activation, retention, referral and revenue

title: How Superhuman Built an Engine to Find Product/Market Fit (Rahul Vohra, 12 November 2018)
supports: Sean Ellis's 'very disappointed' question and 40% benchmark from nearly 100 startups; Superhuman's four questions; score moving from 22% to 33% after segmenting and to 58% within three quarters; half the roadmap on what fans love, half on what holds others back

title: Do Things that Don't Scale (Paul Graham, July 2013)
supports: Recruiting early users by hand; Stripe's 'Collison installation'; Airbnb's founders going door to door in New York; Wufoo's handwritten thank-you notes; narrow starting markets

title: The Mom Test (Rob Fitzpatrick)
supports: The book and its aim: learning from customer conversations without biased feedback, and judging whether someone will really buy

title: SaaS Metrics 2.0: A Guide to Measuring and Improving What Matters (David Skok)
supports: Guideline to recover CAC within 12 months (best 5 to 7); LTV to CAC above 3; net revenue churn above 2% a month loses about 22% of revenue a year; negative churn; cohort analysis by join month; the author calls these guidelines, not hard rules

title: Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing (Ron Kohavi, Diane Tang, Ya Xu)
supports: The standard practical guide to A/B testing, including the overall evaluation criterion (OEC)

title: The Surprising Power of Online Experiments (Ron Kohavi and Stefan Thomke)
supports: Bing's 2012 ad headline idea sat unprioritised for over six months; an A/B test showed a 12% revenue increase, estimated at over $100 million a year in the US

title: How Not To Run an A/B Test (Evan Miller, 18 April 2010)
supports: Peeking and stopping early inflates false positives (26.1% in his worked example against a nominal 5%); fix sample size in advance; rule of thumb n = 16 x p(1 - p) / delta squared

title: Diagnosing Sample Ratio Mismatch in Online Controlled Experiments: A Taxonomy and Rules of Thumb for Practitioners (Aleksander Fabijan et al., KDD 2019)
supports: What a sample ratio mismatch is, that it signals data quality problems, and that ignoring it can make a harmful change look like a win; based on experiments at four companies

title: Retention (Mixpanel Docs)
supports: How retention reports work: starting event and return event, 'on or after' versus 'on' retention, day, week and month buckets, rolling versus calendar mode, and picking a return event that reflects real value

title: Conversions vs. key events in Google Analytics
supports: Key events are the events that matter to the business; a Google Ads conversion is created from a key event and shared between the two products; from 15 June 2026 Consent Mode (within Google Ads) replaced Google Signals as the single control for whether the Analytics tag collects Google Ads cookies and IDs

title: Get started with attribution (Google Analytics)
supports: GA4 offers three models (data-driven attribution, paid and organic last click, Google paid channels last click); first click, linear, time decay and position-based were removed in November 2023; direct visits are excluded unless the whole path is direct; settings sit under Admin > Data display

title: URL builders: Collect campaign data with custom URLs
supports: UTM parameters (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_id, utm_term, utm_content, utm_source_platform); always set source, medium and campaign; values are case sensitive; use lowercase; Campaign URL Builder

title: Consent mode overview
supports: The four consent types (ad_storage, analytics_storage, ad_user_data, ad_personalization); basic mode blocks tags until consent; advanced mode sends cookieless pings while consent is denied and supports more detailed modelling

title: EU user consent policy
supports: Covers end users in the EEA, the UK and Switzerland; sites using Google products must obtain legally valid consent for cookies where legally required and for personal data used for ad personalisation, keep records and explain how to withdraw

title: Update on plans for Privacy Sandbox technologies (Anthony Chavez, 17 October 2025)
supports: Chrome keeps its current approach of offering users a choice on third-party cookies; the Attribution Reporting API, Topics and Protected Audience are retired; an interoperable attribution standard continues at the W3C

title: Guidance on the use of storage and access technologies: What are the exceptions?
supports: ico.org.uk returns 403 to automated fetches, so this exact page was confirmed from search results on 7 Nov 2026 (Decision 8). The Information Commission replaced the ICO on 30 Sep 2026 and still uses the ICO name. Final guidance published 29 April 2026 after the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 changes. The statistics exception covers only aggregate statistics used to improve your own service, with clear information and an easy way to object; it does not cover online advertising or identifying or tracking individuals, and logs or recordings of individual visitors need consent.

title: Data protection and online privacy (cookies section)
supports: In the EU, sites must get consent before installing cookies, except those needed only to transmit a communication or strictly necessary for a service the user asked for; page last checked 5 August 2026

title: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA)
publisher: State of California, Department of Justice, Office of the Attorney General
supports: Right to opt out of sale or sharing for cross-context behavioural advertising; 'Do Not Sell or Share' link; Global Privacy Control must be honoured as an opt-out; applies to for-profit businesses that meet set thresholds; page updated 28 August 2026

title: A Comparison of Approaches to Advertising Measurement: Evidence from Big Field Experiments at Facebook (Gordon, Zettelmeyer, Chapsky, Bhargave; Marketing Science, 2019)
publisher: Kellogg School of Management, Northwestern University
supports: 15 US advertising experiments at Facebook (about 500 million user-experiment observations); common observational methods often failed to recover the effects that the randomised experiments measured

title: Consumer Heterogeneity and Paid Search Effectiveness: A Large Scale Field Experiment (Blake, Nosko, Tadelis; NBER Working Paper 20171, 2014; Econometrica 2015)
supports: eBay field experiments: brand-keyword ads showed no measurable short-term benefit; non-brand ads helped new and infrequent users, but frequent users took most of the spend, so average returns were negative; non-experimental estimates overstated returns

title: Meridian (open-source marketing mix model)
supports: Google's open-source MMM; geo experiments (Meridian GeoX) used as priors to calibrate it; reach and frequency modelling; search query volume to control for organic demand

title: Robyn (open-source marketing mix modelling package)
supports: Meta's experimental, semi-automated, open-source MMM in R (Python API in beta), using ridge regression and budget optimisation

title: The next chapter for 'The Long and The Short of It' (Alison Hoad, 13 September 2023, updated 14 May 2025)
supports: Les Binet and Peter Field's 2013 report found an optimum budget split of about 60:40 brand building to sales activation (62:38 in the 2018 follow-up); warning about over-reliance on short-term metrics; data predates COVID
